thales.name: Thales of Miletus
thales.summary: First brought geometry from Egypt to Hellas; credited via Eudemus with bisecting the circle by its diameter (Def. 17), equality of isosceles base angles (I.5), equality of vertical angles (I.15), and ASA congruence for ship distances at sea (I.26)

mamercus.name: Mamercus (Ameristus)
mamercus.summary: Brother of the poet Stesichorus; remembered in the Eudemian Summary for acquiring great fame through his zeal for geometry

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras of Samos
pythagoras.summary: Transformed geometry into a liberal philosophical discipline, investigating first principles intellectually and discovering cosmic figures and proportionals; credited by tradition with I.47

anaxagoras.name: Anaxagoras of Clazomenae
anaxagoras.summary: Touched upon many questions belonging to geometry after Pythagoras, according to the Eudemian Summary

oenopides.name: Oenopides of Chios
oenopides.summary: Slightly younger than Anaxagoras; first investigated dropping a perpendicular (I.12, calling it kata gnomona) and copying a rectilinear angle (I.23), and distinguished theorems from problems

hippocrates-of-chios.name: Hippocrates of Chios
hippocrates-of-chios.role: Author of the first Elements & squarer of lunes
hippocrates-of-chios.summary: Discovered the quadrature of lunes, pioneered geometric reduction (apagoge, reducing cube duplication to two mean proportionals), and was the first recorded composer of Elements

theodorus.name: Theodorus of Cyrene
theodorus.role: Geometer & teacher of Plato and Theaetetus
theodorus.summary: Eminent in geometry alongside Hippocrates of Chios; famed for proving the irrationality of non-square surds up to 17

hippias.name: Hippias of Elis
hippias.summary: Invented the quadratrix (tetragonizousa) curve used for trisecting rectilinear angles and squaring the circle

protagoras.name: Protagoras of Abdera
protagoras.summary: Argued against geometers that a physical circle touches a straightedge along a line rather than at a single point; refuted by Proclus and cited by Hoenen

plato.name: Plato
plato.summary: Catalyzed the greatest advance in mathematics and geometry; formulated the Divided Line, recollection, analytical method (transmitted to Leodamas), optical straight-line definition, and even-number right-triangle rule

leodamas.name: Leodamas of Thasos
leodamas.summary: Contemporary of Archytas and Theaetetus; received the method of geometric analysis from Plato, discovering many things in geometry

archytas.name: Archytas of Tarentum
archytas.summary: Increased the number of theorems and brought them into a more scientific arrangement alongside Leodamas and Theaetetus

theaetetus.name: Theaetetus of Athens
theaetetus.role: Geometer of irrationals and regular solids
theaetetus.summary: Co-architect of Book X irrationals and Book XIII cosmic polyhedra; honored in the Eudemian Summary

neoclides.name: Neoclides
neoclides.summary: Younger than Leodamas and teacher of Leon; added many discoveries to those of his predecessors

leon.name: Leon
leon.role: Composer of Elements & discoverer of diorismoi
leon.summary: Pupil of Neoclides who composed more careful Elements and discovered diorismoi determining when a sought problem is possible or impossible

speusippus.name: Speusippus
speusippus.role: Nephew of Plato & second scholarch of the Academy
speusippus.summary: Maintained against Menaechmus that all geometric propositions should be called 'theorems' rather than 'problems' because eternal objects have no temporal generation

xenocrates.name: Xenocrates of Chalcedon
xenocrates.summary: Advocated indivisible lines (atomoi grammai), whose geometric impossibility Proclus demonstrates from Prop. I.10 (bisection of every finite segment)

eudoxus.name: Eudoxus of Cnidus
eudoxus.role: Architect of the general theory of proportion & exhaustion
eudoxus.summary: Associate of Plato's circle; first increased the number of general theorems, added three proportions, and extended Plato's inquiries on 'the section' using analysis

amyclas.name: Amyclas of Heraclea
amyclas.summary: Associate of Plato who collaborated in the Academy to perfect geometric science

menaechmus.name: Menaechmus
menaechmus.role: Pupil of Eudoxus & discoverer of the conic sections
menaechmus.summary: Analyzed the dual meaning of 'element' (stoicheion), defended 'problems' alongside 'theorems', and developed the theory of geometric conversion

dinostratus.name: Dinostratus
dinostratus.summary: Applied the quadratrix to the squaring of the circle and perfected geometry in the Academy

amphinomus.name: Amphinomus
amphinomus.summary: Joined Speusippus on theorems vs. problems and collaborated with Menaechmus on the logic of convertible theorems

theudius.name: Theudius of Magnesia
theudius.role: Pre-Euclidean composer of the Academy's Elements
theudius.summary: Arranged the Elements admirably and generalized many partial propositions

athenaeus.name: Athenaeus of Cyzicus
athenaeus.summary: Lived in the Academy with Eudoxus's successors and became eminent in geometry and the other mathematical sciences

hermotimus.name: Hermotimus of Colophon
hermotimus.summary: Pursued the investigations begun by Eudoxus and Theaetetus, discovered many elements, and composed treatises on Loci

philippus.name: Philippus of Medma (Mende)
philippus.summary: Carried out geometric investigations according to Plato's instructions; marks the endpoint of Eudemus's chronicle

aristotle.name: Aristotle
aristotle.role: Founder of the Lyceum & theorist of apodictic demonstration
aristotle.summary: Formulated the epistemology of axioms, postulates, and hypotheses, commensurately universal demonstration, and 'intelligible matter'; critiqued by Proclus on abstraction

eudemus.name: Eudemus of Rhodes
eudemus.role: Peripatetic historian of geometry, arithmetic & astronomy
eudemus.summary: Pupil of Aristotle whose lost History of Geometry is Proclus's primary source for pre-Euclidean geometry, Thales, Oenopides, the Pythagorean angle-sum proof, and application of areas

euclid.name: Euclid
euclid.summary: Synthesized the Elements under Ptolemy I, bringing to irrefutable demonstration what predecessors had proved loosely; revered by Proclus as Platonic by philosophical conviction

archimedes.name: Archimedes of Syracuse
archimedes.summary: Synchronism with Eratosthenes noted at p. 68; cited for shortest-path straight line definition, spirals, Equilibria of Planes, and crown hydrostatics

eratosthenes.name: Eratosthenes of Cyrene
eratosthenes.summary: Cited as contemporary of Archimedes and critic of the nature of proportion as the bond of mathematics

nicomedes.name: Nicomedes
nicomedes.summary: Invented the conchoidal lines (konchoeideis), cited by Geminus and Proclus both for angle trisection and as asymptotic curves that approach a line forever without meeting

apollonius.name: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius.role: The 'Great Geometer' & author of the Conics
apollonius.summary: Transferred Pythagorean application-of-areas terms (parabola, hyperbola, ellipse) to conic sections; proposed alternative proofs for Common Notion 1 and Props. I.10, I.11, I.23

perseus.name: Perseus
perseus.summary: Investigated the three plane sections of the torus (speira), commemorated in an epigram preserved by Proclus

philo.name: Philo of Byzantium
philo.summary: Devised a celebrated direct three-case proof of SSS triangle congruence (Prop. I.8) bypassing Euclid's Prop. I.7

zeno-of-sidon.name: Zeno of Sidon
zeno-of-sidon.role: Epicurean philosopher & foundational critic of Euclid
zeno-of-sidon.summary: Accepted Euclid's principles solely to argue that Prop. I.1 still fails unless one also postulates that two straight lines (or circles) cannot share a common segment

posidonius.name: Posidonius of Apamea
posidonius.role: Stoic polymath & defender of Euclidean foundations
posidonius.summary: Wrote a dedicated treatise refuting Zeno of Sidon; proposed enclosing-limit definition of figure, equidistant definition of parallels, and sevenfold classification of quadrilaterals

geminus.name: Geminus of Rhodes
geminus.role: Stoic mathematician & encyclopedist of the mathematical sciences
geminus.summary: Proclus's richest Hellenistic source on classification of sciences, curves, postulates vs. axioms, uniform flux (quoted in Greek by Hoenen), and asymptotic cautions on Postulate 5

carpus.name: Carpus of Antioch
carpus.summary: Defined angle as distance/divergence between lines and argued in his Astronomical Treatise that problems precede theorems in natural order

heron.name: Heron of Alexandria
heron.summary: Reduced authentic Common Notions to three and supplied direct and construction-sparing proofs for Props. I.19, I.20, I.24, I.25, and I.47

menelaus.name: Menelaus of Alexandria
menelaus.summary: Author of the Sphaerica; contributed a concise direct demonstration of Prop. I.25 (converse Hinge Theorem) preserved by Proclus

ptolemy.name: Claudius Ptolemy
ptolemy.summary: Composed a treatise attempting to prove Euclid's Fifth Postulate; Proclus preserves Ptolemy's lemmas and attempted proof of I.29 while diagnosing its circularity

porphyry.name: Porphyry of Tyre
porphyry.role: Neoplatonic philosopher & commentator on geometric proofs
porphyry.summary: Furnished incisive geometric analyses, case completions, and direct proofs in Book I (Props. I.14, I.18, I.20, I.24, I.26)

iamblichus.name: Iamblichus of Chalcis
iamblichus.summary: Inspired the Athenian Academy's synthesis of Pythagorean-Platonic mathematics in his On Pythagoreanism / De Communi Mathematica Scientia

pappus.name: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus.role: Alexandrian geometer & author of the Collection
pappus.summary: Author of the celebrated zero-construction symmetry proof of Prop. I.5 (pons asinorum) and critical remarks on Postulate 4 converses and additional axioms

plutarch-of-athens.name: Plutarch of Athens
plutarch-of-athens.role: Founder of the Neoplatonic Athenian Academy
plutarch-of-athens.summary: Teacher of Syrianus and aged mentor of young Proclus; cited with reverence on the multi-categorical nature of the angle

syrianus.name: Syrianus
syrianus.role: Scholarch of Athens & Proclus's beloved master ('our Leader')
syrianus.summary: Expositor of ontological projection in phantasia and the horn-angle problem, whose lectures inspired Proclus's Commentary

proclus.name: Proclus Lycius Diadochus
proclus.role: Platonic Successor (Diadochus) & author of the Commentary
proclus.summary: Head of the Athenian Academy for nearly fifty years; composed the Commentary on Book I of Euclid's Elements uniting Neoplatonic epistemology of phantasia, Eudemian history, and rigorous axiomatic analysis

marinus.name: Marinus of Neapolis
marinus.summary: Succeeded Proclus at Athens, wrote Vita Procli, and authored the Preface to Euclid's Data

barocius.name: Franciscus Barocius (Francesco Barozzi)
barocius.role: Venetian mathematician & Latin translator of Proclus
barocius.summary: Published the 1560 Padua Latin edition from Cretan and Venetian manuscripts, healing major corruptions and lacunae of the 1533 Basel Greek editio princeps

taylor.name: Thomas Taylor
taylor.role: English Platonist & first English translator of Proclus on Euclid
taylor.summary: Published the two-volume English translation (1788–1789; reissued 1792) defending Platonic mathematics against modern empiricism

friedlein.name: Gottfried Friedlein
friedlein.summary: Edited the standard 1873 Teubner critical Greek edition from Munich, Vatican, Bologna, and Oxford manuscripts

heath.name: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath.role: Historian of Greek mathematics & translator of Euclid
heath.summary: Author of the monumental three-volume commentary in `geometor/euclid`, citing Friedlein's Proclus at more than 150 loci

hoenen.name: Petrus H. J. Hoenen, S.J.
hoenen.role: Philosopher of geometry & author of De Noetica Geometriae
hoenen.summary: Professor at the Pontifical Gregorian University (`geometor/hoenen`), engaging Proclus on sensible inexactitude, phantasia, intelligible matter, and Postulate 5
